classification.computation: thread CPU >= 80% of wall and in-decision garbage collection < 50% of wall
classification.garbage collection: in-decision garbage collection >= 50% of wall (thread CPU >= 50%)

comparison_rule: gc_in_decision 'paused' disables collection only for the duration of each agent step; decisions cannot change (the probe verifies trace digests against the unpaused games up to the first shot). It is a labelled diagnostic comparison, not a remedy, and none of its figures is reported as the policy's latency.

games.purpose: the configuration of every decision over 1 s
the configuration whose inert seat showed decisions over 100 ms
labelled diagnostic comparison: collection paused inside agent steps

measurements: per decision of every seat: wall (time.perf_counter), thread and process CPU time, components by the external probe, routing requests, Dijkstra runs, nodes settled, distinct start keys, per-unit routing, garbage collections overlapping the decision by generation and duration, resource-usage deltas (page faults, voluntary and involuntary context switches), resident set size
every collection of the oldest generation, with its duration and the decision it fell in, if any
tracked Python objects every 500 decisions (outside the probe window)
load average at the start and end of each game
captured observations: decisions 0-3, every 500th, and every decision slower than 100 ms, for offline replay
not: not an evaluation: no outcome is reported and no game joins an evaluation dataset
no policy, routing, ordering or runtime setting is changed, except the labelled comparison in latdiag-5
no other process on the host is touched, reniced, pinned or suspended
purpose: attribute the rare decision-latency tail of the frozen baseline-v1 observed in baseline-v1-variance-study-1
sessions: one persistent-engine session per game, ledger purpose 'diagnostic'; 5 sessions in total; a failed game is kept and not rerun
